arxiv-2006-16737.title: Delayed Recognition; the Co-citation Perspective
arxiv-2006-16737.creator: Wenxi Zhao, Dmitriy Korobskiy, George Chacko
arxiv-2006-16737.description: Abstract A Sleeping Beauty is a publication that is apparently unrecognized for some period of time before experiencing sudden recognition by citation. Various reasons, including resistance to new ideas, have been attributed to such delayed recognition. We examine this phenomenon in the special case of co-citations, which represent new ideas generated through the combination of existing ones.

arxiv-2104-11586.title: Transverse Confinement of Electron Beams in a 2D Optical Lattice for Compact Coherent X-Ray Sources
arxiv-2104-11586.creator: Arya Fallahi, Niels Kuster, Lukas Novotny
arxiv-2104-11586.description: Abstract Compact coherent x-ray sources have been the focus of extensive research efforts over the past decades. As a result, several novel schemes like optical and nano-undulators for generating x-ray emissions in “table-top” setups are proposed, developed, and assessed. Despite the extensive efforts in the past decades, there exists no operational FEL based on optical or electromagnetic undulators.

arxiv-2105-13974.title: Giant component for the supercritical level-set percolation of the Gaussian free field on regular expander graphs
arxiv-2105-13974.creator: Jiří Černý
arxiv-2105-13974.description: Abstract . We consider the zero-average Gaussian free field on a certain class of finite d d -regular graphs for fixed d ≥ 3 d\geq 3 . This class includes d d -regular expanders of large girth and typical realisations of random d d -regular graphs.

arxiv-2108-09705.title: Observations of cold gas and star formation in dwarf S0 galaxies 2020 Observations of cold gas and star formation in dwarf S0 galaxies –
arxiv-2108-09705.creator: Xue Ge, Qiu-Sheng Gu, Rubén García-Benito, Shi-Ying Lu, Cheng-Long Lei, and Nan Ding
arxiv-2108-09705.description: Abstract Very little work has been done on star formation in dwarf lenticular galaxies (S0s). We present 2D-spectroscopic and millimetre observations made by Centro Astronómico Hispano Alemán (CAHA) 3.5 m optical and the IRAM-30 m millimetre telescopes, respectively, for a sample of four dwarf S0 galaxies with multiple star formation regions in the field environment.

arxiv-2201-12783.title: On a problem of Romanoff type
arxiv-2201-12783.creator: Yuchen Ding
arxiv-2201-12783.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yuchen Ding. Let 𝒫 \mathcal{P} and ℕ \mathbb{N} be the sets of all primes and natural numbers, respectively. In this article, it is proved that there is a positive lower density of the natural numbers which can be represented by the form p + 2 m 1 2 + 2 m 2 2 ​ ( p ∈ 𝒫 , m 1 , m 2 ∈ ℕ ) . p+2^{m_{1}^{2}}+2^{m_{2}^{2}}~~(p\in\mathcal{P},m_{1},m_{2}\in\mathbb{N}). This solves a problem of Chen and Yang in 2014.

arxiv-2212-04559.title: SpeechLMScore: Evaluating speech generation using speech language model
arxiv-2212-04559.creator: Soumi Maiti, Yifan Peng, Takaaki Saeki, Shinji Watanabe
arxiv-2212-04559.description: Abstract While human evaluation is the most reliable metric for evaluating speech generation systems, it is generally costly and time-consuming. Previous studies on automatic speech quality assessment address the problem by predicting human evaluation scores with machine learning models. However, they rely on supervised learning and thus suffer from high annotation costs and domain-shift problems.

arxiv-2308-16246.title: Active Neural Mapping
arxiv-2308-16246.creator: Zike Yan, Haoxiang Yang, Hongbin Zha
arxiv-2308-16246.description: Abstract We address the problem of active mapping with a continually-learned neural scene representation, namely Active Neural Mapping . The key lies in actively finding the target space to be explored with efficient agent movement, thus minimizing the map uncertainty on-the-fly within a previously unseen environment.

arxiv-2401-10123.creator: Venkatesh Mottamchetty, Rimantas Brucas, Anna L. Ravensburg, Renan Maciel, Danny Thonig, Jürgen Henk, Rahul Gupta, Arne Roos, Cheuk Wai Tai, Vassilios Kapaklis, Peter Svedlindh

Ravensburg, Renan Maciel, Danny Thonig, Jürgen Henk, Rahul Gupta, Arne Roos, Cheuk Wai Tai, Vassilios Kapaklis, Peter Svedlindh. arxiv-2402-01979.title: Observation of nonlinear fractal higher-order topological insulator
arxiv-2402-01979.creator: Victor O. Kompanets, Hua Zhong, Yiqi Zhang, Yaroslav V. Kartashov, Yongdong Li, Sergei A. Zhuravitskii, Nikolay N. Skryabin, Ivan V. Dyakonov, Alexander A. Kalinkin, Sergei P. Kulik, Sergey V. Chekalin, Victor N. Zadkov
arxiv-2402-01979.description: Abstract Higher-order topological insulators (HOTIs) are unique materials hosting topologically protected states, whose dimensionality is at least by a factor of 2 lower than that of the bulk. Topological states in such insulators may be strongly confined in their corners that leads to considerable enhancement of nonlinear processes involving such states.

arxiv-2412-12983.title: Exploring natural variation in tendon constitutive parameters via Bayesian data selection and mixed effects models
arxiv-2412-12983.creator: James Casey, Jessica Forsyth, Timothy Waite, Simon Cotter, Tom Shearer
arxiv-2412-12983.description: Abstract Combining microstructural mechanical models with experimental data enhances our understanding of the mechanics of soft tissue, such as tendons. In previous work, a Bayesian framework was used to infer constitutive parameters from uniaxial stress-strain experiments on horse tendons, specifically the superficial digital flexor tendon (SDFT) and common digital extensor tendon (CDET), on a per-experiment basis.

arxiv-2504-00131.title: Gravity in Enhanced Brane-World Models
arxiv-2504-00131.creator: Quim Llorens
arxiv-2504-00131.description: Abstract We generalize and extend results on the localization of gravity on Karch-Randall-Sundrum brane-worlds with positive, negative, or zero cosmological constant on the brane. We do so both from the study of bulk metric perturbations, and from their reinterpretation through brane-world holography —an induced higher-derivative theory of gravity coupled to a cut-off CFT on the brane.

arxiv-2509-08088.title: EnvX: Agentize Everything with Agentic AI
arxiv-2509-08088.creator: Linyao Chen, Zimian Peng, Yingxuan Yang, Yikun Wang, Wenzheng Tom Tang, Hiroki H. Kobayashi, Weinan Zhang, EnvX Team
arxiv-2509-08088.description: Abstract The widespread availability of open-source repositories has led to a vast collection of reusable software components, yet their utilization remains manual, error-prone, and disconnected. Developers must navigate documentation, understand APIs, and write integration code, creating significant barriers to efficient software reuse.

pmc-10526146.title: Fault Reconfiguration in Distribution Networks Based on Improved Discrete Multimodal Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
pmc-10526146.creator: Xin Li, Mingyang Li, Moduo Yu, Qinqin Fan, Heming Jia
pmc-10526146.description: Distribution network reconfiguration involves altering the topology structure of distribution networks by adjusting the switch states, which plays an important role in the smart grid since it can effectively isolate faults, reduce the power loss, and improve the system stability.

pmc-10638179.title: Performance of the FACT-GOG-Ntx to assess chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) in pediatric high risk Hodgkin lymphoma: report from the Children’s Oncology Group AHOD 1331 study
pmc-10638179.creator: Susan K Parsons, Angie Mae Rodday, Qinglin Pei, Frank G Keller, Yue Wu, Tara O Henderson, David Cella, Kara M Kelly, Sharon M Castellino
pmc-10638179.description: BackgroundChemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is an under-recognized complication of several chemotherapy agents used as part of curative-intent therapy for Hodgkin Lymphoma (HL). In the absence of validated self- or proxy-report measures for children and adolescents, CIPN reporting has relied on clinician rating, with grading scales often restricted to severe manifestations.

pmc-10671433.title: Transcriptome Shock in Developing Embryos of a Brassica napus and Brassica rapa Hybrid
pmc-10671433.creator: Weixian Zhou, Libin Zhang, Jianjie He, Wang Chen, Feifan Zhao, Chunhua Fu, Maoteng Li
pmc-10671433.description: Interspecific crosses that fuse the genomes of two different species may result in overall gene expression changes in the hybrid progeny, called ‘transcriptome shock’. To better understand the expression pattern after genome merging during the early stages of allopolyploid formation, we performed RNA sequencing analysis on developing embryos of Brassica rapa, B. napus, and their synthesized allotriploid hybrids.

pmc-11593002.title: Complementary Treatment of Breast Cancer Cells with Different Metastatic Potential with Iscador Qu in the Presence of Clinically Approved Anticancer Drugs
pmc-11593002.creator: Ivan Iliev, Iana Tsoneva, Aleksandrina Nesheva, Galya Staneva, Bozhil Robev, Albena Momchilova, Biliana Nikolova
pmc-11593002.description: European mistletoe extract (Iscador Qu) has been studied for decades, but it has not ceased to arouse scientific interest. The purpose was to investigate the impact of Iscador Qu on the antiproliferative potential of 11 standard chemotherapeutic agents on two breast cancer cell lines: MCF-7 low-metastatic and MDA-MB-231 high-metastatic and control cell lines (MCF-10A).

pmc-11675393.title: The Development of a Certification and Grading Procedure for German SCI Units
pmc-11675393.creator: Rainer Abel, Kerstin Rehahn, Philippe Gorce
pmc-11675393.description: Background/Objectives: Spinal cord injury (SCI) care in Germany was established after the Second World War, following Guttman’s philosophy that post-SCI rehabilitation should not be separated from the acute treatment phase. Reimbursement is negotiated with only rudimentary eligibility requirements. Over time, however, more and more centers have emerged that offer “only” rehabilitation.

pmc-12709512.title: Role of vinegar in cardiovascular health: A narrative review
pmc-12709512.creator: Ridah Ijaz, Raymond Haward
pmc-12709512.description: Background:Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality globally, driven largely by modifiable risk factors, such as hyperlipidemia, hypertension, diabetes, and oxidative stress. As conventional pharmaceutical interventions often carry adverse effects and economic burdens, there is growing interest in alternative therapies.

pmc-13384969.title: Alternative set up strategies for upper tract robotic surgery with the Hugo RAS – experience from an early adopter institution
pmc-13384969.creator: R A Keenan, R Kelly, D Moran, N R Bhatt, K J Breen, B B McGuire
pmc-13384969.description: The Hugo RAS (Medtronic) represents a growing alternative to the DaVinci robotic platform, featuring a distinctive modular arm-cart design that may pose challenges for surgeons transitioning from established systems. Arm-cart positioning, restricted assistant access, and risk of personnel injury have been identified as barriers to adoption.

pmc-13624106.title: Tissue calcinosis in dermatomyositis - potential role of combination therapy with JAK inhibitors. Case report and literature review
pmc-13624106.creator: Paulina Janiak, Żaneta Smoleńska, Anna Wardowska, Michał Chmielewski
pmc-13624106.description: Calcinosis is a disabling and difficult-to-treat complication of adult dermatomyositis (DM), juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM), and systemic sclerosis (SSc), for which no standardized therapy is currently available. Growing evidence implicating JAK/STAT signaling in dermatomyositis has prompted interest in Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) as a therapeutic option.

pmc-13711655.title: The haplotype-resolved T2T genome assembly reveals the evolution and adaptation mechanisms of cold resistance in Rosa beggeriana
pmc-13711655.creator: Huayang Li, Xiang Wang, Yaping Kou, Longzhen Li, Kang Zhang, Xiaofei Wang, Ruidong Jia, Xin Zhao, Hong Ge, Feng Cheng, Shuhua Yang
pmc-13711655.description: rs, several rose genome assemblies have been released, revealing the mechanisms of genomics-based modern rose breeding and ornamental traits [1–3]. Despite the increasing availability of rose genomes, the practical utility of cold tolerance-associated genes unique to wild germplasm remains largely elusive. Our study addresses this gap by presenting complete and haplotype-resolved assemblies for cold resistance mechanisms and adaptation to habitats.
